_doc: Historical target-scope snapshot used to join fungal compound records to Open Enzyme mechanism nodes. Entries are retrieval leads, not a current canonical inventory, rank, or action list. UniProt accessions were used as historical cross-database join keys.
_phase_1_status: historical scope snapshot; all target and source associations require current primary-source rehydration
_historical_redox_scope_note: The original scope collected redox/disulfide-related targets. That collection is retained only as a lead container and does not propose a standalone chokepoint.

uricase_substrate.name: Uric acid degradation (luminal sink)
uricase_substrate.rationale: Historical uricase-substrate search node. Rehydrate source, substrate, compartment, material identity, and direct degradation function.

URAT1.name: Renal urate reabsorption transporter
URAT1.rationale: Historical URAT1 search node. Rehydrate target attribution, effect polarity, substrate, compartment, relevant exposure, and mechanism-matched function.

Lp_PLA2.rationale: Historical Lp-PLA2 search node. Rehydrate source, assay type, effect polarity, relevant exposure, and direct function without inferring personal relevance.

HDAC6.name: HDAC6 (Q141K-ABCG2 trafficking rescue)

NRF2_KEAP1.rationale: Historical Nrf2/KEAP1 search node. Rehydrate exact material, direct target or reporter endpoint, effect polarity, exposure, and downstream function.

OAT1_OAT3.name: Renal organic anion transporters

OAT4.name: OAT4 — apical urate exchanger (renal proximal tubule)
OAT4._historical_scope_note: OAT4 was added to the bounded target scope as an apical urate-exchanger lead. This artifact does not determine its current placement in the canonical wiki.
OAT4.rationale: Historical OAT4 search node. Rehydrate substrate, assay system, effect polarity, concentration, and transporter function.

ADA.name: Adenosine Deaminase — purine catabolism upstream of XO
ADA._historical_phase_5_note: PMID 36385640 was recorded as an ADA-associated GLPP lead. The retained record does not establish direct ADA inhibition, causal attribution to a GLPP component, or current chokepoint status.
ADA.rationale: Historical ADA search node. Rehydrate exact composition, assay type, direct ADA function, effect polarity, exposure, and attribution controls.
ADA.rehydration_gate: Inspect the primary material and assay, then test direct ADA function and urate-pathway consequences before any propagation or comparison.

_PRELIMINARY_PINK1_mitophagy.name: PINK1 / mitophagy historical lead
_PRELIMINARY_PINK1_mitophagy.rationale: PMID 40334761 was recorded as a Cordyceps cicadae, PINK1/mitophagy, and hyperuricemia-nephropathy retrieval lead. It does not establish a current chokepoint or component-level mechanism.
_PRELIMINARY_PINK1_mitophagy.rehydration_gate: Verify the material, PINK1/mitophagy endpoint, causal attribution, model scope, and connection to inflammasome function before any current claim.

_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads.name: Redox/disulfide-related historical lead container
_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads._status: lead only; not a proposed, admitted, preliminary, or rejected chokepoint
_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads._scope_boundary: The bounded searches and later narratives cannot support a universal presence or absence claim for this mechanism space.

candidate_targets.name: ergothioneine biosynthesis (fungal-side)
candidate_targets.rationale: Fungal-side biosynthesis lead, not a human target; producer identity and product yield require source verification.

_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads.rationale: Historical redox/disulfide identifiers are retained only to support source rehydration and mechanism-specific testing.
_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads.rationale_for_retention: Retain identifiers and search leads so exact compound–target records can be rehydrated without treating the historical scope as a decision.
_HISTORICAL_redox_disulfide_leads.rehydration_gate: Verify compound identity, fungal provenance, direct target function, effect polarity, relevant exposure, and mechanism-matched downstream consequences.
